title: exec-staff-meeting-prep-notes-priya-2026-03-29
body:
Exec staff meeting — prep notes (Priya)
Date: 2026-03-29
Time: 10:00-11:00 PT
Attendees: CEO, CTO, COO, VP Eng, VP Product, Head of SRE, Head of Sales, Head of Customer Success
Meeting goal: Align on top production risks, Dedicated rollout status, new pricing pilot decision, and 90-day priorities for reliability and cost optimization.

Top-line context (quick bullets for CEO/CTO):
- Hosted API Q1 usage +22% MOM; revenue-weighted token volume up ~18%. Growth concentrated in embeddings/semantic search workloads.
- P50 latency for text-generation endpoints drifted from 85ms to 120ms last week during peak windows (see notes). Root cause likely batching backpressure + a kernel fallback on one GPU class.
- Dedicated onboarding: 4 customers in pilot; 2 are green, 1 has networking/KMS issues, 1 requested higher throughput than current pool. Still on track for beta next month but need a patch for autoscaler.
- Private deployment (regulated customer): deployment delayed due to policy review (infosec) and HSM integration timeline. Sales asks for clearer delivery dates.

Prepared agenda (25m topics + 15m decisions + 20m Q/A):
1) Reliability/Risk (10m) - Head of SRE
   - Quick summary of latency spike, mitigation steps taken, and timeline for permanent fix.
   - Request: approve follow-up engineering time to harden the batching allocator (est. 2 engineers x 2 weeks).
2) Dedicated & Private rollout status (8m) - VP Eng + Solutions Eng
   - Pilot health, blockers, autoscaler patch ETA, capacity plan for next 90 days.
   - Decide: pre-commit additional 50% burst capacity for pilot customers?
3) Pricing pilot for high-throughput embeddings customers (7m) - VP Product
   - Proposal: tiered per-embedding unit pricing + SLA option. Need leadership sign-off to run pilot with 3 anchor customers.
4) Sales escalation: regulated customer timeline + expectations (5m) - Head of Sales
5) Ops ask: emergency on-call rotation + follow-on deer/incident docs (5m) - Head of SRE

Key metrics snapshot (latest available):
- API requests/day: 1.1M (avg), +22% MOM
- Embedding units/day: 420k, +35% MOM
- Revenue-weighted token volume: +18% MOM
- P50 Latency (generation endpoints): 120ms (peak window), baseline 85ms
- Error rate (5xx): 0.6% (up from 0.3%)
- Dedicated pilot capacity utilization: 68%

Open issues / background (short):
- Latency spike: observed correlated increase in queue time on node class g4x-16 during 11:00-13:00 PT. Early RCA: one kernel path fell back to a slower GEMM after recent kernel library upgrade. Patch tested in staging; needs smoke in canary.
- Autoscaler: current logic insufficient for bursty embedding jobs; Solutions Eng built prototype. Needs product sign-off for safety constraints.
- Private/HSM: third-party HSM vendor requested updated SOC2 attestation copies; legal and security are coordinating.

Decisions required at meeting:
- Approve 2 engineers x 2 weeks for batching allocator fix (cost: ~$30k equivalent) - Owner: Head of SRE
- Approve temporary +50% burst capacity allocation for Dedicated pilot to avoid throttling (cost to be charged to pilot budget) - Owner: VP Eng
- Approve running pricing pilot with 3 anchor customers (marketing collateral + legal review) - Owner: VP Product

Proposed action items (clear owners + due dates):
- Head of SRE: schedule canary rollout of kernel patch and report back with perf numbers by 2026-04-02.
- VP Eng: confirm burst capacity availability and update capacity plan by 2026-04-01.
- Solutions Eng (Miguel Torres): provide short runbook for autoscaler behavior and guardrails by 2026-04-05.
- VP Product: finalize pricing pilot landing page + legal template with Sales by 2026-04-06.
- Head of Sales: send commitment timelines to regulated customer and propose 2 delivery windows by 2026-03-31.
- Priya Raman (me): coordinate exec comms + follow-up doc and publish meeting notes to Confluence by 2026-03-30.

Follow-ups I want from leaders (post-meeting):
- CTO: prioritize kernel compatibility test coverage in CI (what is the rough ETA to include the risky kernel paths?).
- COO: confirm whether additional contingency budget is available for Dedicated burst capacity this quarter.
- VP Eng: plan for 30/60/90 day milestones for Dedicated capacity scale (short slide, 1 page).

Unresolved questions / risks to surface in meeting:
- If latency root cause is broader than kernel fallback (e.g., unexpected workload pattern), what is plan B? Can we throttle or route to another region with acceptable latency?
- Legal: any blockers with the proposed pricing pilot language re: revenue recognition or discounts?
- Sales: do we have authority to promise specific delivery windows to regulated customers given security review dependencies?

Notes for CEO (quick talking points):
- We expect to contain the latency regression via a quick kernel patch + canary within 1 week; long-term CI coverage will reduce recurrence risk.
- Dedicated is progressing; asking for modest burst allocation to avoid losing pilot momentum - this has clear ROI via conversions.
- Pricing pilot is low-risk and helps us collect elasticity data; recommend greenlight.

Raw scratchpad / possible phrasing for decisions section in meeting doc:
- "Approve allocation of up to 50% additional Dedicated burst capacity for pilot customers for the next 60 days, charged to pilot budget. VP Eng to report usage and cost weekly."
- "Approve funding for short-term engineering work to harden batching allocator (2 engineers x 2 weeks). Head of SRE to lead and deliver canary results."

Attachments & refs (for meeting):
- Perf graphs (P50/P90) - link in Confluence (attached in meeting invite)
- Autoscaler prototype doc: ENG-1427 (link above)
- Customer escalation email thread (Sales) - link in Slack thread above

Quick personal TODO after meeting:
- Publish notes to Confluence + tag owners (due 2026-03-30).
- Drop a quick CEO summary email with three bullets and next steps.
- Follow up with Head of SRE on canary schedule to ensure no overlap with major deployments.

Tone: concise, prioritization-first; call out resourcing needs and customer-risk items early so CEO can weigh trade-offs.

-- end of notes --
